summary: This work presents an error budgeting and suppression procedure for the echo cross-resonance (ECR) gate on an OQC Toshiko Gen-1 32-qubit superconducting processor, identifying and mitigating control-qubit leakage, $I\hat{Z}$ coherent errors, and background $ZZ$ interactions through pulse-shaping and compensating gates. Applied to a 16-qubit chain, the procedure achieves a 3.7× reduction in two-qubit gate error rates, improving the median error from 4.6% to 1.2% as measured by interleaved randomized benchmarking, with the largest improvements on previously under-performing pairs.
motivation: Larger superconducting QPUs exhibit a broad distribution of two-qubit gate qualities across qubit pairs due to fabrication uncertainties in qubit frequencies and frequency-dependent error sources, creating a low-performing tail that limits near-term quantum algorithms and error correction.
method: Error sources were systematically characterized via repeated $T_1$ and $T_2^e$ measurements, leakage amplification circuits, and quantum process tomography; control-qubit leakage was suppressed using single-derivative DRAG pulses; $I\hat{Z}$ errors ($\sim 2.3\%$ mean error-per-gate) were corrected with virtual-$Z$ rotations; $Z\hat{Z}$ errors ($\sim 0.4\%$ mean) in four problematic pairs were further suppressed using target-qubit $R_Y$ compensating pulses.
result: Median error per gate on the 16-qubit chain decreased from 4.6% to 1.2%; mean error improved from 6.75% to 1.6%; incoherent error ($0.3\%$–$0.8\%$) and unexplained error ($0.6\%$ median after suppression) now dominate over coherent and leakage errors, indicating that further improvements require faster gates relative to coherence times $T_1 \sim 69$ µs and $T_2^e \sim 103$ µs.
